name: AIKeyboard async typing corpus
notes: Async-tier exam. Same shape as Bar/typing/corpus.json, plus optional pauseMs and screen.
pauseMs is the idle the PredictiveRefiner is asked after. The local 72/76 headline does not include these entries.
Foundation Models cannot predict Hebrew. A Hebrew next-word skip is measured, not a corpus failure.
were is not in the contraction table. apos-09 is this tier's named job.

NIT-21: mustNotCorrect entries added below, exercised through a pause for the first time. An entry where the right answer is to leave the bold slot alone is scored exactly as it is in Bar/typing/corpus.json (commit = bold slot still equals what was typed); a corpus made only of improvable cases flatters the refiner.
apos-09-control and apos-10-control pair a risky word with a context where the async-only correction must NOT fire, the same word as its improvable twin either way.

The Hebrew entries below (he-no-correct-*, he-comp-01, he-next-02/03, he-async-screen-01) are still expected-skip: PredictiveRefiner.standard never carries a Hebrew-capable engine (see .claude/rules/suggestion-bar.md). They are here to prove the skip is graceful at a larger, more varied sample than one entry, not to claim Hebrew prediction works.
First run needs a machine where Foundation Models actually answers (see Bar/typing/async/run.sh); nothing in this file has been scored against the model yet.

entries.probes: were is a common word. The local tier must leave it alone; the sentence is the async tier's job.
Trigram with essentially one continuation.
Several good answers (tomorrow, soon, there); tests spread, not a single hit.
Idiom completion where the literal reading is much weaker.

screen.message: Are you free for lunch tomorrow?

entries.probes: Empty field, a question on screen. The async tier is the only thing that can see it.
The Hebrew equivalent of Happy ___. Foundation Models cannot predict Hebrew; a skip here is measured, not a corpus failure.
English mid-word with a pause. Local already has tomorrow; the model should not replace it with something else.
Stem shared by approve, approval, approved; context favours the noun. A second English mid-word pause.
Apology frame; delay, confusion, late are all defensible.
Strongest bigram in the language; a blank bar here is disqualifying.
Short prefix already typed, a question on screen. The model can see both.
wed is an ordinary word (to marry) and not in the contraction table; only the sentence says it means we'd.
shed is a real word (garden shed) and not in the contraction table; the sentence forces the contraction reading, the same shape as apos-09 and apos-10.
Same risky word as apos-09, opposite context: were is the correct past-tense verb here and must not become we're. Checks the refiner is reading the sentence rather than pattern-matching the word.
shed here is the noun, not she'd; pairs with apos-11 the way apos-09-control pairs with apos-09.
Common given name, not in any dictionary. A paused version of the local corpus's nc-05/nc-06 class: the async tier must not have its own opinion about names.
A digit paused mid-thought; nothing should happen, sentence-level or not. Paused twin of the local corpus's nc-07.
Two-letter real word autocorrect likes to capitalise or expand into OK/Okay; must survive a pause too. Paused twin of the local corpus's nc-03.

entries.context: Let me know if you have any
entries.probes: Common closing request; several good nouns, tests spread rather than a single hit.
Idiom completion; several natural closes.
Near-fixed idiom; essentially one continuation.
Stem shared by postpone/postponed; context after 'get' favours the participle.
Stem shared by confirm/configure/confess; 'I need to' strongly favours confirm.

screen.message: Can you send the deck before the call?

entries.probes: Empty field, a request on screen. A third screen-context entry so this class is not a sample of one shape.
Good night idiom (laila tov). Expected-skip class, same as he-next-01: Foundation Models cannot predict Hebrew.
Thank you very much (toda raba). Expected-skip class, same as he-next-01.

Arriving, mid-word with a pause. The local tier already handles this well (see .claude/rules/suggestion-bar.md); this checks the async path over the same ground does not make it worse, in the same spirit as en-comp-tomor.
Complete two-letter Hebrew word, paused. Paused twin of the local corpus's nc-08: the async tier does not serve Hebrew at all, so this must stay a local-only pass even with a pause armed.
Product name in the shipped personal dictionary; must survive a pause too, and Hebrew's async skip must not somehow let a different word through.
Hebrew screen context; extends the expected-skip class to the screen-aware path rather than only plain next-word.
